comment: Generated by runtime/http/go/paging (cd runtime/http/go && go test ./paging -run TestWriteParityVectors -update); do not edit. The Go, TypeScript and Rust HTTP runtimes each run every vector through their page reader and builder (D60): paging.Parse, paging.EncodeCursor, paging.DecodeCursor and paging.FromRows in Go; readPage, encodeCursor, decodeCursor and pageFromRows in TypeScript; PageSpec::query, Cursor::encode, Cursor::decode and Page::from_rows in Rust. reads: spec is an operation's @paginated limits and query a raw query string, which the runtime parses as its router does, WHATWG's form-urlencoded parser: pairs split at & alone, + a space, a % that starts no escape kept as it is; the reader answers request, the cursor (null for none) and the limit, or refuses it with problem, the 400's status, code, detail and details, compared as JSON values. cursors: keyJSON is a key as compact JSON, its objects' members in sorted order and its numbers small integers or short decimals, so every runtime writes it back the same; cursor is what encoding it gives, and decoding cursor into a JSON value gives keyJSON's value. refused: decoding cursor into a JSON value is refused with problem. unencodable: encoding the key keyJSON fails, the implementation's error, since every router would refuse its cursor. fromRows: rows are JSON values, each its own key; building a page of them for limit gives page, items and next (null for none), as the page's JSON. A sorted operation (D60, amended): a read's spec.sort is its SortBy argument, the query parameter param, the fields, and default, @paginated's defaultSort, and request.sort the sort read, as its text (-placedAt), absent for an unsorted spec; the reader is the router's whole read, Go's paging.Parse, TypeScript's readPage and Rust's PageSpec::query then PageSpec::unbind, so a sent cursor is unbound and request.cursor is the implementation's own. bindings: binding the implementation's cursor under sort (paging.BindCursor, bindCursor, Cursor::bind) gives bound, the unpadded base64url of exactly the bytes {"sort":"<sort>","key":<the key's JSON as cursor holds it>}, and unbinding bound under sort gives cursor back. refusedBindings: unbinding cursor under sort (paging.UnbindCursor, unbindCursor, Cursor::unbind) is refused with problem. unbindable: binding cursor under sort fails, the implementation's error: its key's cursor is not one the encoder writes, or the bound cursor would be past 1024 characters.
